resumen: On a bench inclined to about 30°, the dumbbells open in an arc to the sides with the elbows slightly bent and come back together over the upper chest. An isolation exercise for the chest.
ejecucion: Sit with a dumbbell on each thigh and lie back, bringing them to your chest before straightening your arms.
Set the back rest to about 30° and lie back with a dumbbell in each hand, arms straight over your upper chest and palms facing each other.
Bend your elbows slightly and keep them that way throughout.
Open your arms in an arc to the sides until your elbows reach shoulder level, and no further.
Come back along the same arc until the dumbbells meet over your chest.
If you feel a pull at the front of your shoulder, open less or lower the weight.
matices: We have found no study measuring incline flyes themselves. In the press, an inclination of about 30° was the one that most activated the upper chest in a study of thirty people; it is reasonable to think flyes behave similarly, but it has not been measured. At the bottom, with the arms open, the shoulder is in a demanding position; that is why it is usually advised not to go below shoulder level, which on an incline bench is a clearer limit than the bench itself.
